problem: World-model-based navigation planners (e.g. NWM+NoMaD) are verification-centric two-stage pipelines: an external policy samples candidate trajectories, a world model rolls them out, and the best match to the goal is picked. This makes them dependent on candidate coverage, very slow, and prone to geometrically inconsistent rollouts.
motivation: Decoupling goal intent from trajectory synthesis wastes compute and leaves spatial reasoning implicit in visual patterns. Navigation needs goal-aligned, spatially feasible paths in one pass, so jointly generating what to perceive and how to act, with depth cues, should be more accurate and efficient.
key_idea: Fine-tune a pretrained video diffusion transformer (CogVideoX) to jointly denoise intermediate RGB-D latents and action tokens conditioned on start and goal frames, with depth pseudo-labels used only in training, a visual-guided action refinement module, and a trajectory-scale regularization loss.
insight: Joint generation of observations and actions gives large gains even without extra modules: the CogVideoX joint baseline already beats NWM on TartanDrive ATE (4.90 vs 6.23). The ablation shows TSR fixes long-horizon drift (TartanDrive ATE 4.90→2.63) and depth adds spatial grounding, and the two are complementary (RECON ATE 1.70→1.01 when TSR is added to depth). VGAR gives a further small gain on most datasets.
method: Joint RGB-D + action diffusion: fine-tunes the CogVideoX DiT to denoise one token sequence of intermediate RGB latents, depth latents and action tokens (DDPM-style), conditioned on start and goal RGB/depth latents.
Latent tokenization: a frozen CogVideoX 3D VAE encodes RGB and depth maps separately; 2D planar actions (Δx, Δy) are embedded by a learnable MLP into the same token space.
Depth pseudo-labels: DepthAnything V3 provides per-frame depth during training only; inference needs just monocular RGB start and goal images.
VGAR (Visual-Guided Action Refinement): gated residual cross-attention where final-layer action tokens attend to visual tokens before the action head decodes them.
TSR loss: L_TSR = ||Σ a_n − p_G||₂ / N, supervising the cumulative displacement to the goal; total loss is L_DDPM + λ·L_TSR.
Zero-initialized new modules: new parameters start at zero so the model initially behaves like the pretrained video generator and progressively learns the coupling.

setting.backbone: CogVideoX DiT (fine-tuned) with a frozen 3D VAE, plus VGAR module
setting.training_data: RECON, SCAND, TartanDrive navigation trajectory datasets (NWM protocol), with DepthAnything V3 depth pseudo-labels; HuRoN is held out for zero-shot evaluation
setting.observation: monocular RGB start and goal images (depth used only at training)
setting.action_space: planar displacement sequences (Δx, Δy) over a horizon of 8 steps (9 frames)

numbers.eval_set_note: NWM standardized evaluation subsets; average of three runs

results: SWAM reduces ATE versus NWM+NoMaD (×16) by 39.2% on RECON, 47.2% on SCAND and 75.1% on TartanDrive, and runs in 16.91 s per episode versus 245.98 s. It also has the best PSNR/SSIM on all three datasets and, zero-shot on HuRoN, gets ATE 2.94 versus 3.73 for a baseline trained on HuRoN.
limitations: Misidentifies traversable weeds as obstacles because the model has no semantic traversability reasoning.
Planar (Δx, Δy) actions omit orientation, so sharp turns are handled poorly.
Evaluated only offline on trajectory datasets (no closed-loop or real-robot tests); the horizon is short (8 steps), and it is still about 17 s per episode.
